procedural_matters: SWE 34 was represented by Carl Ljunggren (crew).
GER 79 was represented by Reamonn Theiner (helm).
The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
Riccardo Honold (crew of GER 49) gave evidence as a witness.
facts: The conditions at the time of theincident were 4 knots of wind with slightly choppy sea state.
When the boats were on the leg between mark 1 and 2, the wind shifted 30 degrees to the right.
SWE 34 and GER 79 gybed from starboardto port tack at a distance of 6-7 boat lengths to mark 2.
SWE 34 was overlapped to leeward ofGER 79 and half a boat length to the front.
When SWE 34 entered the zone of mark 2, she wasoutside overlapped to GER 79.
SWE 34 bore away at the distance of half a boat length to mark 2.
conclusions: SWE 34 outside overlapped at the zone gave mark-room to GER 79, and complied with her obligations under RRS 18.2(a)(1).
